title: How to become a data engineer in 2026
summary: Discover the steps and skills needed to become a successful data engineer. Start your journey toward a rewarding career in data engineering.
body_markdown:
- [Intuit Blog](https://www.intuit.com/blog)


- [All Posts](https://www.intuit.com/blog/all-posts/)


- [Innovative Thinking](https://www.intuit.com/blog/hub/innovative-thinking/)


- How to become a data engineer in 2026


If you want to become a data engineer, you’re aiming for a job that few people get straight out of school. Most learn skills in a set order and take a first job close to the data.


This guide covers the job, the pay, what to learn first, and six steps to get hired. It also shows how the path changes based on where you start.


## Key takeaways


- Most people become data engineers in steps. They start with a degree, an internship, or a nearby role like data analyst or software engineer, then move into data engineering work.
- SQL and Python come first. A 365 Data Science analysis of 703 data engineer job posts, updated April 2026, found SQL in 79.4% of them and Python in 73.7%.
- Federal job data files data engineers under database architects. That group earned a median of $139,500 in 2025, and BLS projects 9% job growth from 2025 to 2035.
- A bachelor’s degree is the usual path, but not the only one. About 23% of the job posts in that analysis didn’t list a degree.
- Certifications help most after you’ve built something. AWS and Google both recommend years of hands-on experience before their data engineer exams.


## What is a data engineer?


A[data engineer](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/what-is-a-data-engineer/) builds the systems that collect, clean, and store a company’s data. Other teams use that data every day. Analysts, data scientists, and AI tools all depend on it.


The U.S. government doesn’t track data engineer as its own job. The federal[O*NET database lists “Data Engineer”](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/15-1243.00) as a job title under database architects, so that’s the group used for pay and job outlook in this guide.


Data engineering is often compared with[software engineering](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/data-engineer-vs-software-engineer/) . It also overlaps with the work of a[data scientist](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/data-engineer-vs-data-scientist/) .


## What do data engineers do?


A data engineer’s day varies by team, but most handle these core duties:


- Building data pipelines: Imagine a pipeline that takes raw data from various sources and transforms it into a clean, usable format. Data engineers design and build these pipelines to automate the flow of data.
- Managing data infrastructure: They’re responsible for setting up and maintaining the databases and data warehouses that store all this data. This ensures the data is secure, reliable, and accessible.
- Ensuring data quality: Inaccurate or incomplete data is not useful. Data engineers make sure data is clean and consistent by checking for errors and inconsistencies.
- Designing data architecture: Data engineers plan how to structure and organize data. This helps streamline how teams store, retrieve, and analyze data.


This work takes care, because a single pipeline may pull data from many sources and each one has to line up.


Once a pipeline is built, it mostly runs on its own. Alerts warn the team when something looks wrong, but the hard part is what alerts can’t fix: a source system changes its format, a job fails overnight, or a report shows numbers nobody trusts. Some data engineering jobs include on-call rotations to fix those problems fast.


## Why become a data engineer?


Data engineering pays well, and the field is growing. Here’s what federal data shows for database architects, the group that includes data engineers:


- Median pay: $139,500 a year in May 2025, according to the[Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/database-administrators.htm) .
- Pay range: the lowest-paid 10% earned under $86,240 and the top 10% earned over $204,000, per the same BLS data.
- Job growth: BLS projects 9% growth for database architects from 2025 to 2035.


Pay still varies a lot by company, location, and level.


The work itself is another draw. Data engineers solve hard problems every day, and many find that rewarding.


Data is also one of a company’s most valuable assets. It drives big decisions, speeds up daily work, and sets the stage for new products. Data engineers make that possible, so their work has a clear impact.


That demand reaches small businesses too, as more of them run decisions through AI. Regular AI use among the US businesses surveyed for the[2026 Intuit QuickBooks AI Impact Report](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/r/small-business-data/ai-impact-report/) rose from 48% in July 2024 to 77% by January 2026. Those tools depend on clean, reliable data, and data engineers build it.


Small businesses rely on that data as well: Brandon Littleton, who runs the restaurant Bag Ladies with his brother, checks its profit and loss statement in QuickBooks every day. On the Mind the Business podcast, he explained how seeing those numbers, like when they were spending too much on food, let them adjust quickly:


> Just having that information in front of us helped us make more informed decisions.
>
>
> Brandon Littleton, who runs the restaurant Bag Ladies with his brother, on “[Using Data to Shape Your Future](https://omny.fm/shows/mind-the-business-small-business-success-stories/using-data-to-shape-your-future) “


Data engineers also work across many industries. O*NET lists professional, scientific, and technical services and finance and insurance as the top industries for database architects.


## Skills required to become a data engineer


So what skills does the job take?


Data engineers need both technical skills and soft skills. Here’s what to learn in each group:


Technical skills:


- Programming: SQL and Python matter most. A[365 Data Science analysis of 703 data engineer job posts](https://365datascience.com/career-advice/data-engineer-job-market/) , updated April 2026, found SQL in 79.4% and Python in 73.7%. Java and Scala showed up in fewer posts.
- Databases: Understanding relational databases (like MySQL and PostgreSQL) and NoSQL databases (like MongoDB and Cassandra) is crucial for storing and managing data.
- Big data and streaming tools: Apache Spark appeared in 41.1% of the posts in that study and Apache Kafka in 16.2%. Hadoop, an older big data framework, appeared in 17.8%.
- ETL and orchestration: Data engineers build extract, transform, load (ETL) pipelines to move data between systems. ETL skills appeared in 57% of the posts. Tools like Apache Airflow schedule and run those pipelines.
- Cloud computing: Most jobs expect it. Cloud platforms like Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) all appeared often in the study’s job posts.


Soft skills:


- Problem-solving: Data engineers tackle complex challenges. Strong problem-solving skills are essential for designing and troubleshooting data pipelines.
- Communication: Effective communication with both technical and non-technical audiences is crucial for collaboration and explaining complex data concepts.
- Teamwork: Data engineering often involves collaboration with data scientists, analysts, and software engineers. Teamwork is essential for project success.


## What to learn first: a data engineering roadmap


The skills above work best in order. Each one builds on the last. Here’s the order we’d follow:


1. SQL: Learn to query, join, and summarize data. It’s the skill almost every data engineering job asks for.
2. Python: Use it to pull data from files and APIs, clean it, and load it somewhere else.
3. Data modeling: Learn how to plan tables so data stays clean and easy to search.
4. Pipelines: Turn your scripts into jobs that run on a schedule, using a tool like Airflow. Add checks that catch bad data.
5. Cloud: Pick one platform. Learn how it stores and processes data.
6. Big data and streaming: Add Spark or Kafka once your basic pipelines work.


Then build one project that covers the whole path, from raw data to a clean table someone could use. Step 3 below shows how.


## How long does it take to become a data engineer?


The answer depends on your path. Most people take one of two routes: a college degree, or a shorter course like a certificate program.


If you go the traditional route, it can take[four to five years](https://www.datacamp.com/blog/how-to-become-a-data-engineer) to become a data engineer. This path typically starts with a bachelor’s degree in computer science, IT, mathematics, or a related field. Students will also want to accumulate as much real-world experience through internships and other programs as possible during this time.


A degree isn’t the whole story, though. O*NET puts this work in its “Job Zone Four” group. It says most of these jobs require a bachelor’s degree, “but some do not.” The same group usually calls for several years of work-related experience, on-the-job training, or vocational training. That’s why many people move into data engineering from another job, like data analyst or software engineer.


You can also find courses that teach data engineering without a degree. These take weeks or months instead of years. They work best for people who already know some basics, have a related degree, or can’t attend college.


The key with these classes is to choose a well-known program whose projects you can show to employers. A course alone may not be enough to land a job, so plan to pair it with a portfolio or a related role.


## How to become a data engineer: 6 steps


Becoming a data engineer is a great goal. But where do you start? Follow these six steps.


### 1. Get data engineering education


First, pick the education path that fits you. Think about the kind of job you want, then work backward. Does it call for a four-year degree, or could an online course get you there?


You can even find online data engineering courses from universities. For example, the University of Chicago offers an eight-week online data engineering course that earns continuing education units.


### 2. Grow your data engineering skills


Work through the skills in the roadmap above, starting with SQL and Python. Then add a data warehouse, a cloud platform, and a pipeline tool. Practice on real data as you go. Employers look for skills you’ve used on real work.


Technical skills are easy to find classes for. Soft skills are what set you apart.


So build your problem-solving and communication skills too. Data engineers don’t work alone. You’ll work on big projects with people across the company, like project managers and business analysts. Learning to explain your work clearly will help you at every step.


### 3. Build a portfolio


Employers want proof you can do the work. A portfolio shows them.


Start with one pipeline that runs from start to finish. Pick a public dataset you care about. Pull it in with Python, clean it, and load it into a database. Then set it to run on a schedule. Add a check that flags bad data, and write a short note that explains your choices. One finished pipeline beats a list of half-built ones.


You can also freelance or volunteer to add real projects. Sites like Upwork and Freelancer list freelance work. Our guide to building a[data science portfolio](https://www.intuit.com/blog/social-responsibility/job-readiness/data-science-portfolio/) covers where to host your work.


### 4. Consider an internship


An internship gives you real work experience. Some pay and some don’t. Either way, you’ll gain the experience employers look for.


Start looking once you have a few portfolio projects. Job sites like LinkedIn, Indeed, and Glassdoor list openings.


### 5. Grow your network and find a mentor


A mentor who already works in the field can speed up your path. You can learn from their experience, ask questions, and get one-on-one feedback.


Where do you[find a mentor](https://www.intuit.com/blog/life-at-intuit/people-culture/finding-a-mentor-when-where-and-how/) ? Local conferences and meetups are a good place to start. Search social media or meetup sites to find groups near you.


### 6. Search and apply for data engineering jobs


Now it’s time to apply. Today’s job market is competitive, so tailor each resume to the job you want.


Use your network too. People you know can tell you about open roles at their companies, and a referral from an employee can make a big difference.


A simple way to sharpen your resume is to leave out education or work experience that doesn’t relate to the job. Many employers use[applicant tracking systems](https://www.library.hbs.edu/working-knowledge/how-to-tap-the-talent-automated-hr-platforms-miss) to sort applications, so match your resume’s wording to the skills the job post lists.


Post your portfolio on LinkedIn or a personal website, so you can link to it in every application.


## Do you need a data engineering certification?


No, but one can help you stand out once you have hands-on skills. Each major cloud company has a data engineer certification:


Certification Exam fee Recommended experience


[AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate](https://aws.amazon.com/certification/certified-data-engineer-associate/) $150 2 to 3 years in data engineering or data architecture, plus 1 to 2 years with AWS


[Google Cloud Professional Data Engineer](https://cloud.google.com/learn/certification/data-engineer) $200 3+ years of industry experience, including 1+ year on Google Cloud


[Microsoft Fabric Data Engineer Associate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/fabric-data-engineer-associate/) Varies by country Intermediate level


[Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate](https://www.databricks.com/learn/certification/data-engineer-associate) $200 None required; training recommended


Microsoft retired its older Azure Data Engineer Associate certification on March 31, 2025. Check that any course you take prepares you for a current exam. If you’re new to the field, build your first pipeline before you pay for one.


## How to become a data engineer as a student or career changer


Your next move depends on where you’re starting. The deciding factor is whether you can get paid work near data while you learn.


### For students


Use your school years to land an internship near data or software work. Paid programs exist. Intuit’s[internship and co-op program](https://www.intuit.com/careers/programs/internships/) connects students with real projects across software engineering, data, design, and more, and its programs are paid. Its US summer internships run 12 weeks. Our guide on[how to get a data science internship](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/how-to-get-data-science-internship/) covers the application side.


### For career changers


Look for a paid way into tech first. Then grow into data work. Apprenticeships are one route. Intuit’s[Career Pathways](https://www.intuit.com/careers/programs/career-pathways/) program is a paid, ten-month software development apprenticeship that requires no prior technical experience, and apprentices who successfully complete it receive an offer for a full-time role at Intuit. It’s open to US applicants only. It isn’t a data engineering program, but the software skills carry over.


Not sure where you fit? Use the starting-point map below.


If you’re starting as Aim for this first role Learn next First project


A student An internship or entry-level software or data role SQL, Python, one cloud platform A scheduled pipeline built on a public dataset


A[data analyst](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/data-analyst-vs-data-engineer/) or BI developer An analytics engineering role, or more pipeline work on your current team Python, data modeling, orchestration Automate a report you now build by hand


A software engineer A move to a data platform or backend data team Advanced SQL, data modeling, Spark or Kafka A streaming pipeline with data quality checks


A career changer from outside tech An apprenticeship, a bootcamp, or an analyst role SQL first, then Python Clean and load one messy dataset you know well


## Find data engineering jobs at Intuit


You now have the skills, the order to learn them in, and the steps to get hired. When you’re ready, browse[data jobs at Intuit](https://www.intuit.com/careers/teams/data-science/) to see open roles.


## Frequently asked questions about becoming a data engineer


### Do you need a degree to become a data engineer?


Usually, but not always. Most data engineering jobs ask for a bachelor’s degree, but about 23% of the 703 job posts in the 365 Data Science analysis didn’t list one. O*NET also says most jobs in this group require a bachelor’s degree, “but some do not.”


### What programming language should a data engineer learn first?


Start with SQL, then Python. SQL appeared in 79.4% of the job posts in the 365 Data Science analysis and Python in 73.7%.


### How much do data engineers make?


Federal data groups data engineers with database architects, who earned a median of $139,500 a year in 2025. The lowest-paid 10% earned under $86,240 and the top 10% earned over $204,000.
